Aitareyāraṇyaka
also called RgvedAraNyaka an. AraNyapaJcaka (RASB. II. 205). Ṛv. Āśval. in five books; the first three books form the original text; traditionally ascribed to the seer of the Brāhmaṇa, Aitareya Mahidāsa, who is mentioned in the text (II. 1. 8, 3. 7). Āśvalāyana is the a. of Āraṇyaka IV according to the tradition recorded by Ṣaḍguruśiṣya, (C.. Macdonell, Sarvānukramaṇī, p. xix; an. NCC. II. p. 214a); Sāyaṇa repeatedly states that Śaunaka is the a. of Āraṇyaka V, also known a. Sūtrāraṇyaka (C.. Sāyaṇa's C. on Ṛv. 1. 8. 1 an. the beginning of his C. on Āraṇyaka V of Aitareya. See Intro. [Page083-a. to Keith's edn. of Ait. Āraṇyaka, p.. 18 ff. Adhy.. 4-6 of Āraṇyaka Two form the Aitareyopaniṣad; the seventh ch. forms its Śāntipāṭha. Sometimes the whole of Āraṇyaka Two is called Ait. Up. or Mahaitareyopaniṣad or Bahvṛcabrāhmaṇopaniṣad. See notes under Ait. Upaniṣad.

Aitareyopaniṣad
also called AtmaSaTkopaniSad, bahvRcabrAhmaNopaniSad or bahvRcopaniSad an. AtmopaniSad (See TD. 906). Ṛv. See also NCC. II. p.. 58a, 214b, Ātmaṣaṭkaº an. Āśval. Up. Adhyāyas 4-6 of Ait. Āraṇyaka Two form the Ātmaṣaṭka, an. the term Ait. Up. is generally restricted [Page084-b] to this part; the seventh adhyāyaforms the Śāntipāṭha. Sometimes the whole of Āraṇyaka two is taken a. the Upaniṣad an. called Bahvṛcabrāhmaṇopaniṣad or Mahaitareyopaniṣad. Āraṇyaka three called Saṁhitopaniṣad is sometimes taken a. part of Ait. Up. See Keith's Oxford edn. of the Ait. Āraṇyaka, Intro. p.. 39-52. Ānandatīrtha an. his Dvai. followers take the whole of Āraṇyakas Two an. Three a. the Up. an. among adv. writers Upaniṣad Brahmendrayogin has commented on the whole of Āraṇyaka Two an. there are mss. of Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya for the entire portion of Āraṇyakas Two an. Three.
